title: Direct Recovery of Examination Documents
description: Draft public-service guidance; review questions must be resolved before publication.
clarifying_questions: Is the missing or spoilt item a result slip, certificate or another examination printout?
Which examination and release or dispatch year applies?
Was the document never received, lost after collection, spoilt, or printed with incorrect details?

claims.text: The historical manual describes recovery of missing or spoilt results slips, certificates and examination printouts.
The public query page directs examination queries through heads of institutions and Sub-County Directors of Education.

citations.locator: Period Of launching queries after release of Results

claims.text: The public query page separately describes recovery queries for certificates and result slips, including incorrect candidate or centre details and cases where a document was not received. This service must not be presented as replacement of a certificate lost after collection.

citations.locator: Query on Recovery of Certificates; Query on Recovery of Results slips

claims.text: The 2018 QMIS guide uses Direct Recovery as its example: choose Direct Recovery, complete the generated form, confirm the captured details and attachments, submit, verify success feedback and track the query through Status.

citations.locator: PDF p5 section2.1 steps2-4 and pp5-6 sections2.2-2.3

claims.text: The 2026 charter says certificate queries should be raised within 60 working days after dispatch of certificates; this does not establish a universal deadline for lost certificates or every type of printout.

Direct recovery concerns missing or spoilt examination documents. A person who lost a certificate after receiving it must be routed to the separate Examination Results Certification Letter service, not promised a recovered or replacement certificate through this article.

unresolved_questions: Confirm current eligibility, attachment and payment requirements separately for result slips, certificates and printouts.
Confirm the triggering event for certificate-recovery deadlines and any examination-specific exceptions.
Preserve the boundary between direct recovery and certification after loss.
